tasks.short: Gather requirements, clean and import asset and parts data, set up maintenance plans, test with real jobs and train mechanics.

steps.what: Supervisor gathers requirements with mechanics, planners and the manager
Supervisor cleans asset and spare-part lists from old spreadsheets row by row for import
Supervisor sets up preventive maintenance programs per asset in the system
Application specialist configures the system, integrations and reports
Supervisor tests the setup with real job orders
Supervisor trains mechanics to use the system

tasks.design: Import scripts written with AI coding help by the application specialist load the old spreadsheets into the maintenance management system ({OTHER}), with validation rules that flag duplicates, missing fields and unknown asset types for the supervisor to fix. Preventive plans are built once per asset type and copied to similar assets; requirements, testing and training stay with the supervisor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Data migration meant weeks of manual clean-up, so systems went live half-filled.
tasks.enabler_now: AI coding speeds up import scripts and integrations, and maintenance systems support plan templates per asset type.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing the maintenance strategy and getting mechanics to use the system are people work; one documented system was poorly adopted because of its interface.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which assets matter and making the system fit how the team actually works.

ambition.what: Preventive plans in place for every critical asset at go-live, not added over years.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor fixes flagged data and shapes plans instead of retyping lists.

reach.task: Schedule preventive work from the new plans
reach.learn: Whether templates per asset type give workable schedules.

evidence.claim: An enterprise asset management system offers downtime reporting, failure-mode maintenance strategies and ERP links.
A food maker with 12 production sites reported about 30% less downtime after moving to preventive work in such a system (vendor case, no baseline).
A maintenance system that logs mechanics' work can monitor performance and needs works council consent.
AI coding tools speed up writing import scripts and integrations.

assumptions: Boundary: from requirements to mechanics trained; vendor selection is outside.
Input contract: old asset and part lists from spreadsheets; asset types and validation rules agreed by the supervisor and planner; fallback is manual entry.
Application specialist time is outside the supervisor's savings.
Requirements, testing and training do not change.
unknowns: Number of assets and part numbers to migrate.
research_questions: How many flagged rows need human fixing per thousand imported?

already_counted.description: Supervisor reviews and fixes rows flagged by validation.

incremental.description: Supervisor keeps asset type templates current.
Application specialist maintains import scripts and integrations.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Plants with few assets or clean data save little on migration; very messy data still needs long manual fixing.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Talk with mechanics about their needs, measure, sketch the equipment layout, check ergonomics, list parts, get approval and oversee installation.

steps.what: Supervisor talks with mechanics about what they need at the workstation or in the van
Supervisor measures the space and the equipment
Supervisor sketches the equipment configurations on paper
Supervisor checks ergonomics and safety with the safety advisor
Supervisor makes the equipment and parts list and asks suppliers for prices
Supervisor oversees installation and adjusts it with the users

tasks.design: A simple layout tool with a library of the plant's standard benches, racks and van inserts drawn to scale replaces paper sketches, and the equipment list with article numbers comes from the items placed. Needs, measuring, ergonomics checks and installation stay with the supervisor and users.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each layout was sketched by hand and the parts list typed separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Layout tools with equipment libraries are widely available and cheap.
tasks.still_hard: Each team's needs differ; the library only covers standard items.
tasks.human_edge: Listening to mechanics and building a workplace they want to work in.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; drawings and lists are quicker.

reach.learn: Whether the shared library standardises van fit-outs.

evidence.claim: Layout tools with scaled equipment libraries can produce a parts list from the items placed.
Workplaces must be designed with attention to ergonomics under national working conditions rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from user needs to installed equipment; buying is done by purchasing outside this task.
Input contract: equipment library with dimensions and article numbers built by the supervisor from suppliers' data; fallback is paper sketches.
Manager and safety advisor time is outside the supervisor's savings.
Talks, measuring, checks and installation do not change.
unknowns: How often equipment configurations are redesigned.
research_questions: Do standard layouts cut installation changes afterwards?

incremental.description: Supervisor adds new equipment items to the library.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: One-off configurations with custom equipment gain little from a library.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The maintenance supervisor shapes systems and workplaces with the team; data clean-up and drawing take less time.
skills_to_grow: Building plan templates per asset type
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who brings a new maintenance system live with clean data and full preventive plans.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
